transcript.content: Hello, I’m glad you came in today. What brings you in today?

When I have to sit and focus on these long claim files, my mind just checks out and I end up putting them off or staring at the screen instead of getting them done. It's really starting to impact my performance at work, and I'm just feeling pretty stuck.

Have problems with attention, procrastination, or restlessness been present since childhood and in more than one setting, like school or home, or did they start more recently after stress or mood changes?

They've actually been around since I was a kid, and my elementary school teachers used to write comments on my report cards about me daydreaming, forgetting homework, and losing worksheets. I managed to get by through high school and community college by cramming and relying on my memory, but it became a major problem recently when my job switched to a high-volume, metrics-driven workflow.

Besides work, do these attention and organization problems also affect other parts of your life now, like paying bills, keeping appointments, managing chores, or relationships? If so, which areas are most affected?

Yes, they definitely affect other parts of my life, especially when it comes to keeping appointments. I’ve missed a couple of dentist appointments because I’ll see the reminder earlier in the day and think "I'll remember that," but then I get wrapped up in something else and completely forget about it until hours later.

Do you also have symptoms like feeling restless, fidgeting, talking excessively, interrupting others, or acting before thinking? Or are your difficulties mainly with attention, forgetfulness, and organization?

My main struggles are definitely with attention and organization, but I do experience some physical restlessness like constantly bouncing my leg or clicking my pen. I often get too antsy to stay seated during long meetings and will find excuses to get up and walk around, though I don't really struggle with talking excessively or interrupting others.
Have these attention problems been present even during times when you were not depressed, overly anxious, or using substances, and do they clearly interfere with your work or daily life?

Yes, these issues have been there since childhood, long before any work anxiety started, and I don't have depression or use substances. They've seriously interfered with my job—I've been written up twice, missed out on a promotion, and I'm constantly terrified I'm going to get fired over my errors and unfinished files.
